title: Exact localization preserves a nested adjunction mate
statement: Let A,B,C be abelian categories with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let L:B→A, R:A→B, L2:C→A, R2:A→C and T:B→C be additive functors preserving finite limits and finite colimits, with adjunctions a1:L⊣R, a2:L2⊣R2 and a natural isomorphism c:R⋙T≅R2. Let d1:LD1⊣D(R), d2:LD2⊣D(R2) be any chosen derived left adjoints. For a complex K of A, an object E of D(A), and e:QK≅E, let p1:LD1(D(R)E)≅Q(L(RK)) and p2:LD2(D(R2)E)≅Q(L2(R2 K)) be the concrete derivedPresentation isomorphisms: leftAdjointUniq to the localized termwise adjunction, followed by e and the mapDerivedCategoryFactors isomorphisms. Suppose f:L2(R2 K)→L(R K) is a complex map whose component in each degree n is the a2-transpose of c(K^n)⁻¹≫T(η1(R K^n))≫c(L R K^n). Form cD:D(R)⋙D(T)≅D(R2) by the exact-functor composition isomorphism and D(c), and κ as the d2-transpose of cD(E)⁻¹≫D(T)(ηd1(D(R)E))≫cD(LD1 D(R) E). Then p2.hom≫Q(f)=κ≫p1.hom. The statement has no cover or exact-sequence hypothesis and asserts no distinguished triangle.

proof.text: Apply the termwise adjunction on complexes. Its unit and counit components are exactly the original unit and counit in each degree, so the componentwise assumption identifies f with the termwise nested mate by complex extensionality. Localize this identity at quasi-isomorphisms, which all five functors preserve by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

Expand the localized unit and counit on QK using Mathlib Adjunction.localization_unit_app and localization_counit_app (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Adjunction.lean:118,127). Use the composition and natural-isomorphism factorization identities mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac to replace the localized comparison by cD. Cancel consecutive inverse factorization maps. This gives the asserted equation for E=QK and the localized adjunctions.

Naturality carries the equation along e:QK≅E. The chosen adjunctions are compared with the localized ones by leftAdjointUniq. Its unit and counit compatibility equations carry the mates to each other, yielding the asserted equation with the concrete p1,p2. All these transports are isomorphisms, so no fullness of Q on morphisms is required.

theorem derivedPresentation_mate
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C]
    {L2 : C ⥤ A} {R2 : A ⥤ C} {T : B ⥤ C}
    [L2.Additive] [R2.Additive] [T.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits L2] [PreservesFiniteColimits L2]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits R2] [PreservesFiniteColimits R2]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits T] [PreservesFiniteColimits T]
    (a1 : L ⊣ R) (a2 : L2 ⊣ R2) (c : R ⋙ T ≅ R2)
    {LD1 : DerivedCategory B ⥤ DerivedCategory A}
    {LD2 : DerivedCategory C ⥤ DerivedCategory A}
    (d1 : LD1 ⊣ R.mapDerivedCategory) (d2 : LD2 ⊣ R2.mapDerivedCategory)
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) {E : DerivedCategory A} (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E)
    (f : (L2.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        ((R2.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ⟶
      (L.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        ((R.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))
    (hf : ∀ n, f.f n = (a2.homEquiv _ _).symm
      (c.inv.app (K.X n) ≫ T.map (a1.unit.app (R.obj (K.X n))) ≫
        c.hom.app (L.obj (R.obj (K.X n))))) :
    letI : PreservesFiniteLimits (R ⋙ T) := comp_preservesFiniteLimits R T
    letI : PreservesFiniteColimits (R ⋙ T) := comp_preservesFiniteColimits R T
    let cD := (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso R T).symm ≪≫
      Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso c
    let κ := (d2.homEquiv _ _).symm
      (cD.inv.app E ≫ T.mapDerivedCategory.map
        (d1.unit.app (R.mapDerivedCategory.obj E)) ≫
        cD.hom.app (LD1.obj (R.mapDerivedCategory.obj E)))
    (a2.derivedPresentation d2 K e).hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map f =
      κ ≫ (a1.derivedPresentation d1 K e).hom
